scope: Cloud task SSE replay boundary, terminal lifecycle, and cache resource bounds
finding: The hub used separate locks for sender registration and history replay, permitting a publish to appear in both replay and live delivery. Completed tasks retained up to 512 events and a broadcast sender indefinitely, and terminal streams did not close.
change: A shared hub-state mutex makes subscribe and publish atomic across history/live boundaries. Replay is bounded to 512 events and 256 KiB per task; frames above 64 KiB are rejected and untrusted error/remote identifiers are shortened before serialization. Completed cache is capped at 128 tasks and 30 minutes, terminal senders are released, submit/cancel terminal paths close streams, and the HTTP SSE handler ends after replaying a terminal event.
regression_test_source: 300 concurrent subscribe/publish handoff iterations assert a frame is delivered exactly once
completed-task capacity, per-task history byte cap, and oversized frame rejection
live receiver closure and late HTTP replay stream closure after terminal event
unknown task ids return a closed receiver without allocating a retained sender

rust_tests.required: at least 6 GB available and memory use strictly below 80%

limitations: The new concurrency tests, cache eviction logic, Cloud HTTP lifecycle wiring, and real SSE disconnect behavior have not been type-checked or executed by Rust.
